text:
alex: Heads-up — new RFP for a financial customer asking about running Redwood in a fully disconnected datacenter. They want operator-based installs, a predictable upgrade cadence, and clear pricing for offline bundles. Can we confirm what we can offer?

maria: +1. Core asks: 1) packaging format (operator vs immutable bundle) 2) patch cadence (monthly/quarterly?) 3) signed artifact workflow and activation keys 4) pricing add-on for offline support.

sam: For packaging we support both: a k8s operator for day-2 ops and an immutable tarball for strictly air-gapped sites. Operator requires cluster access during install; immutable bundle can be installed with a single offline bundle + activation key.

joanne: Important constraint from legal: any offline bundle needs SBOM and signed provenance for CVE auditing. We also need a cert rotation doc for on-prem KMS integration.

ryan: From infra side: delta patches are possible but only via signed patch bundles; we don’t allow running unsigned diffs. Typical cadence customers ask for: monthly security patches, quarterly feature rollouts. We can offer a locked cadence (quarterly) for customers who want a slower change window.

alex: What's the recommended default for a cautious bank customer? Monthly security + quarterly feature?

sam: Yes. Recommend monthly security-only patches + quarterly full-bundles. That keeps risk low and lets them opt into more frequent fixes.

maria: Logistics Q: do we require a new activation key for each bundle, or can they reuse a site token?

ops-bot: deploybot: Note — offline activation supports both per-bundle short-lived keys and long-lived site tokens. Long-lived tokens are blocked for high-risk customers; default is per-bundle key.

joanne: For the contract we should offer two pricing lines: 1) base license + on-prem platform fee 2) offline-support SOW (includes bundle signing, SBOM, test validation, 24/7 patch delivery). POC pricing can be free for 30 days if hosted; for air-gapped POC we charge a fixed packaging + validation fee.

ryan: Technical ask — need to know allowed egress for bundle validation. If no egress at all, we do pre-sign everything and include verification keys in the bundle. If limited egress, we can do a CRL/checkin stub.

alex: Can someone paste the offline install snippet we give customers?

sam: Sure — example bootstrap we give ops teams:

```
# bootstrap offline bundle
redwoodctl install --bundle /tmp/redwood-offline-2026-01.tgz \\
  --activation-key xxxxx-REDACTED-xxxxx \\
  --sbom /tmp/sbom.json \\
  --verify-signature /tmp/signature.sig
```

sam: Also note: for operator installs we include a controller image in the bundle and a CRD manifest with pinned image digests; upgrade happens by applying a new signed bundle which updates the CRD image fields.

maria: Action items: sam to draft packaging options doc + sample SOW, joanne to draft pricing line items, ryan to outline test matrix for no-egress installs. We should aim to send a response to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

alex: Great — thanks all. If any blockers (legal, signing infra), call them out in thread. :thumbsup:
